figures.caption: Table 1: Overall performance comparison of base models and their MBP-KT-enhanced counterparts across three datasets. Bold indicates the better result within each baseline-enhancement pair. ↑ indicates higher is better; ↓ indicates lower is better.

Figure 1: The comparison between MBP-KT and previous methods. (a) Conventional KT models only leverage the individual responses for prediction. (b) Prior collaborative KT models rely on the behavior match through the raw interaction sequences to extract the collaborative information for serving the specific model. (c) MBP-KT transforms raw sequences into meta-behavioral sequences to extract the global collaborative features for enhancing the performance of diverse KT models.
Figure 9: The t-SNE visualization of learner representations derived from meta-behavioral sequences on three datasets (K=3).

Figure 10: Attention weight matrices of the baseline AKT (left), the enhanced AKT+MBP-KT (middle), and their point-wise difference (right). The difference map (Ours - Baseline) highlights the suppression of local recency bias (blue, negative) and the activation of long-range dependencies (red/orange, positive).
Figure 2: The overall architecture of MBP-KT.
Figure 8: Visualization of learner-to-learner similarity matrices derived from collaborative representations (sorted by 3 clusters). (a) ASSISTments2009. (b) EdNet-KT1. (c) XES3G5M.
Figure 7: Visualization of collaborative representations’ heatmaps across datasets. (a) ASSISTments2009. (b) EdNet-KT1. (c) XES3G5M.
Figure 4: Sensitivity analysis of window size N and sequence length K.
